A Linux shell, a browser, MCP servers and skills, and, with Hands on, the apps on your phone and the windows on your computer through their screens, for everything that never had an API.		 Asks first.

Reaches your other devices.
Say it on the phone, it runs on your PC; @Mac … at the start of a message sends the task there. Approvals come back to the device in your hand.		 Keeps going.
Goals checked on a schedule, routines that run while the app is closed, a feed written for you each morning.
Remembers you.
What it is, what it knows about you and when it wakes are Markdown files you can read and edit.		 Lives in your chat apps.

A look of its own.
Describe one, your image model draws it, a video model makes it move. A small dragon by default.		 Any model.

<title>nanoMuse 1.0.5 · Lookout</title>
<content type="html"><h1>nanoMuse 1.0.5 · Lookout</h1>
<p>🐉 <strong>nanoMuse <code>1.0.5</code> “Lookout”</strong>: the day after Compass, a second look at the whole project together with the day's reports; the daily feed is written out of sight, the Android approval card fits the screen, the desktop's dead buttons work and a quit protects the work in progress, the Windows release can update itself, and the relay's console finds anything.</p>
<p>1.0.4 went out on 2026-10-13. The same day we read nanoMuse through once more, this time with the reports and pull requests that arrived while Compass was being built, and nine passes again went over the relay, the Python runtime, the web console, the desktop, the Android and iPhone apps, the hosted showcase, the documentation and the workflows (<a href="https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/444" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/444/hovercard">#444</a> to <a href="https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/455" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/455/hovercard">#455</a>). What they found fills this version. Some of it you will see at once: the chat the daily feed is written in no longer sits in your chat list on any device, and a routine's turn opens with its result; a long command no longer pushes the Android approval card's buttons off the screen (<a href="https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/436" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/436/hovercard">#436</a>, reported by @HBSTAR0501); the ChatGPT sign-in on a phone with a proxy has a way through (<a href="https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/441" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/441/hovercard">#441</a>, reported by @Kooooooo-G); the iPhone's conversation scrolls under the header, Siri understands the app's phrases in nine languages, and an emoji face set on the desktop shows on the phone (<a href="https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/435" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/435/hovercard">#435</a>, reported by <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/Yousanflics/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/Yousanflics">@Yousanflics</a>); eight desktop buttons that quietly did nothing do their job again, and quitting the desktop asks before it ends a reply, a hands run or a task another device is waiting on. # Open Dots: Open-Source Alternative to Paid AI Agents

**Open Dots is an open-source, self-hosted alternative for people exploring
paid AI agent products such as OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse, Grok Bot, Instinct,
Manus Cue, Claude Cowork, and ChatGPT agent.** The current prototype focuses
on coding-agent workflows: run Claude Code tasks from Telegram or the web,
review risky actions, connect GitHub, and schedule recurring prompts. Its
features differ from those services; it is not a feature-for-feature
replacement.

Both interfaces use the same API, sandbox, and credentials for each user.

## What it does

- Run coding-agent tasks in disposable sandboxes from Telegram or a browser.
- Connect Claude through its OAuth login flow and optionally connect a user's GitHub account.
- Ask for approval before risky actions such as file writes, shell commands, and Git pushes.
- Continue completed tasks in the same Claude conversation from the web UI.
- Schedule recurring prompts and receive run results in Telegram.
- Store user credentials encrypted and manage sandbox, task, permission, and schedule records in PostgreSQL.

### Prerequisites

- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for Python dependency management
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) (20.9+) and npm, for the web UI (required by Next.js 16)
- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) (for Postgres; not needed with the experimental SQLite option, see `DATABASE_BACKEND` below)
- Bash (Git Bash on Windows works fine) to use `scripts/dev.sh`
